reason: The narrative predominantly centers on King David's experience as he confronts multiple sources of opposition and disloyalty. Absalom's rebellion directly challenges his rule; Shimei curses him and questions his legitimacy (16:7-8); Ahithophel, his trusted counselor, joins the conspiracy against him. Throughout chapters 13-19, the text depicts David navigating these crises—his grief over his son's betrayal, his tactical responses to rebellion, his emotional anguish. While the narrative is in third-person (not first-person), it is fundamentally organized around David's perspective on events and his struggle with those who oppose his authority.
